audit: VERTEX Kattis original statement evidence ledger — pass 11
method: Water and Fire were inspected in their original contest problem-set PDFs. Train Sorting was inspected via a secondary judge mirror that identifies Waterloo 2008 Spring A; this does not prove the exact submitted contest date.

records.title: Water
records.statementTitle: 2016 ACM ICPC Southeast USA Regional Division 1, Problem J — Water
records.identity: Original 2016 SEUSA Division 1 contest PDF contents list Water on page 12 and provide the exact water-company pumping station/mansion statement.
records.observed: A water utility network has bidirectional pipes with capacities. Across a sequence of permanent improvements, it increases existing pipe capacities or installs new pipes. After every improvement, report the maximum water flow from pumping station to mansion.
records.excerpt: A water company is trying to provide water from its pumping station to a mansion.
records.inputOutput: Input: stations, initial pipes and a sequence of capacity increases/new pipes. Output: maximum flow after initial setup and after every improvement.
records.constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 100; p ≤ n(n−1)/2; 1 ≤ k ≤ 10,000; pipe capacities and increments ≤ 1,000.
records.scenarioAssessment: Strong contextual scenario: real utility-network setting, evolving network state, repeated operational queries, capacity constraints and max-flow objective. Strong candidate for long-scenario qualification, subject to final rubric consistency review.

records.title: Fire
records.identity: Original BAPC 2012 problem set identifies Problem F Fire and includes the building-fire escape statement matching Kattis fire2.
records.observed: A person is trapped in a building with spreading fires and walls. Fire advances every second; the person must reach an exit without entering a cell that is burning or about to burn, with simultaneous escape allowed.
records.excerpt: You are trapped in a building consisting of open spaces and walls. Some places are on fire and you have to run for the exit.
records.inputOutput: Input: multiple building maps containing rooms, walls, one person and fire sources. Output: minimum escape time or IMPOSSIBLE.
records.constraints: At most 100 test cases; width and height each from 1 to 1,000.
records.scenarioAssessment: Clear emergency-response context and interacting time-dependent hazards, but a single well-defined multi-source BFS escape problem. Moderate scenario candidate; not automatically long-scenario approved.

records.title: Train Sorting
records.identity: DMOJ identifies the task as Waterloo 2008 Spring A, with statement and constraints matching Train Sorting. This corroborates the year/source family but not the submitted exact June 15 date.
records.observed: Erin arranges arriving train cars by adding each new car to the beginning or end of a train, or rejecting it. The resulting train must be ordered by weight and as long as possible.
records.excerpt: Cars arrive at the train station in a predetermined order. When each car arrives, Erin can add it to the beginning or end of her train, or refuse to add it at all.
records.inputOutput: Input: number of cars followed by distinct car weights. Output: maximum possible train length.
records.constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 2,000; weights are nonnegative and distinct.
records.scenarioAssessment: The 2008 Waterloo provenance is now corroborated by an independent judge mirror. The narrative is short and the task is a single LIS-style optimization; not a strong long-scenario candidate.
